tools.name: close_composition
tools.description: Closes a composition and removes it from the user's tabs. Use it to clear up attempts you made along the way — an agent that leaves ten of them behind has handed the user the tidying. Needs an explicit id; it will never guess the active one.

tools.name: connect
tools.description: Pairs you with a Motion browser tab. The user has an eight-character code on screen, under the Connect MCP button — something like K7M4-P2Q9. Call this once at the start. tools.description: Starts a Motion session WITHOUT the user having a tab open. Use this when they have no pairing code — you can create and edit compositions immediately, and give them the returned link when they want to watch. Ask them to open the session link, then call this instead of asking them to tell you when it is ready. It returns as soon

tools.name: tell_user
tools.description: PUT A SENTENCE ON THEIR SCREEN, as you work. They are watching the Motion tab while you build, and between your tool calls it shows nothing — a busy agent and a hung one look identical from there. Call this at every step that takes more than a few seconds: what you are about to do, what just landed,

tools.name: read_skill
tools.description: Motion's authoring guides. Read {topic:'motion'} first — it is the API contract: what compiles, what resolves, what renders. Then {topic:'motion-craft'} ALWAYS before writing a line, because the API guide alone produces compositions that render correctly and look generated. 'motion-text' for typogra

tools.name: list_media
tools.description: The user's media library: folders, and files with id, name, kind, size and folder. `storage` says whether a file is 'linked' (still on their disk) or 'copied' (held by the browser) — a linked file can need the user to re-grant access after a reload.

tools.name: put_media
tools.description: Adds a file to the library from a URL — the BROWSER fetches it, so nothing travels through this connection, but it only works on https hosts that send CORS headers. tools.name: get_media
tools.description: The raw bytes of one file, base64. Capped at about 600 KB — for anything larger, and for every video, use inspect_media instead: it answers what is IN the file for a fraction of the size.

tools.name: inspect_media
tools.description: Looks INSIDE a file. Returns ONE contact sheet — every requested moment as a labelled cell in a single grid image. Pass atSec (up to 12 timestamps, seconds); omit it for an even spread across the whole clip. This is how you analyse a video second by second without paying for a dozen separate images.

tools.name: organize_media
tools.description: Library housekeeping. action: 'move' (ids + toFolder), 'delete' (ids), 'createFolder' (name + optional parent), 'deleteFolder' (folder — the files inside move up one level, nothing is lost).

tools.name: list_compositions
tools.description: The compositions open in the tab, and which one is on screen.

tools.name: get_composition
tools.description: One composition in full: manifest, every source file, and current prop values. Read this before update_composition so you edit what is actually there.

tools.name: create_composition
tools.description: Writes a new composition and opens it as a tab in front of the user. `files` maps path to TSX source and must include the entry (default composition.tsx). tools.name: update_composition
tools.description: Edits an existing composition. `files` is MERGED by path, so send only what changed. Changing the schema keeps any prop values that still have a home.

tools.name: set_props
tools.description: Sets prop values on a composition — the same values the user's controls change. Merged, so you can send one key.

tools.name: inspect_composition
tools.description: LOOK AT WHAT YOU MADE. Renders frames of a composition and returns them as one labelled contact sheet. Puts the composition on the user's stage and plays it from frame 0 through the real preview — the path a person watches, which inspect_composition does not take — from the first frame to the last. findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "connect" references sensitive artifacts (session token). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_skill · Private data: connect, list_media, put_media, get_media, inspect_media, organize_media, get_composition, create_composition, update_composition, inspect_composition · Public sink: create_session, put_media, update_composition, set_props, inspect_composition · Destructive: put_media, organize_media, check_playback, get_problems.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_skill · Private data: connect, list_media, put_media, get_media, inspect_media, organize_media, get_composition, create_composition, update_composition, inspect_composition · Public sink: create_session, put_media, update_composition, set_props, inspect_composition · Destructive: put_media, organize_media, check_playback, get_problems

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
